item.title: Building a Highly Available Chatbot With OmniPaxos
item.description: The OmniChat chatbot. See it in action on YouTube . Consensus protocols play a key role in providing fault tolerance in distributed systems. They allow multiple servers to coordinate their operations and behave as a single system that continues operating even when some servers fail. However, consensus protocols are notoriously difficult to understand and implement correctly. As a result, fault tolerance is typically provided through separate consensus-based services, such as key-value stores1, databases2, and block storage3.

item.title: Building distributed RocksDB with OmniPaxos in 8 minutes
item.description: In this post, we will demonstrate how to use OmniPaxos to build a simple distributed database. As seen in the Figure below, we will go from a single-server database service to a distributed setup with multiple servers replicating the database. OmniPaxos will act as the replicated changelog for the distributed database that provides a single execution order for all replicas so they remain consistent. overview. Currently, the client and server are executed in separate docker containers and communicate over TCP sockets.

item.title: How OmniPaxos handles partial connectivity - and why other protocols can’t
item.description: State machine replication (SMR) protocols such as Raft, VR, and MultiPaxos are widely used to build replicated services in the cloud. These protocols depend on a stable leader to make progress. However, as shown by the 6+ hour Cloudflare outage in 2020, partial connectivity can cause the leader election in these protocols to fail. In a previous post by Howard and Abraham, they showed how Raft overcomes some partial connectivity scenarios by incorporating new logic into the leader election process.
